'''Pavel Exner''' (born 30 March 1946 in [[Prague]]) is a Czech [[mathematical physics#Mathematically rigorous physics|mathematical physicist]].<ref name="homepage">[http://people.fjfi.cvut.cz/exnerpav/ ''Pavel Exner's homepage: http://people.fjfi.cvut.cz/exnerpav/'']</ref>

== Life ==
Born on March 30, 1946, in Prague, his parents were Vilem Exner, economist, and Marie, born Karvankova, ophthalmologist. He graduated in 1969 in theoretical physics from the [[Charles University]] in Prague.<ref name="personal">[https://people.fjfi.cvut.cz/exnerpav/personal.html ''Pavel Exner's personalia'']</ref>

After working at the Charles University as an assistant professor, he moved in 1978 to the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]], [[Dubna]] in Russia. Due to peculiarities of the time he had no doctoral advisor and got his PhD only in 1983; still in Dubna he also got the higher doctorate in mathematical physics in 1990.<ref name="personal"/> 

Back to his home country in 1991 he became head of a mathematical-physics group in the [[Nuclear Physics Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences|Nuclear Physics Institute AS CR]] of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="personal"/> In 2003 he became professor of the [[Charles University]]. Since 2006 he works as the Scientific Director of the Doppler Institute for Mathematical Physics and Applied Mathematics at [[FNSPE CTU]] in Prague.<ref>[http://doppler.fjfi.cvut.cz/ ''Doppler Institute'']</ref>

Since 1971 he is married to Jana, born Wiendlova, physicist. They have three daughters and five grandchildren.<ref name="personal"/>

== Scientific work ==
His scientific interests concern in the first place mathematical problems and methods of quantum theory, in particular, unstable systems and resonances, scattering theory, functional integration, and quantum mechanics on graphs, surfaces, quantum waveguides.<ref name="personal"/><ref name="board"/> 

His best known results include existence of curvature-induced states in quantum waveguides, solvable models of quantum systems with contact interactions, and the theory of leaky quantum graphs.<ref name="board"/>

He was awarded various prizes,<ref name="personal"/> among them JINR Prize in theoretical physics and the Neuron Prize for outstanding contributions to science.<ref>[https://www.nfneuron.cz/en/scientists/pavel-exner ''The Neuron Fund'']{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> In 2010 he was elected member of [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>[http://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Exner_Pavel ''Academia Europaea'']</ref>

His bibliography includes several books and more than two hundred research papers.<ref>[http://gemma.ujf.cas.cz/~exner/listpub.pdf ''List of publications'']</ref> His best known results include existence of curvature-induced states in quantum waveguides, solvable models of quantum systems with contact interactions, and approximations of vertex couplings in quantum graphs.

== Professional service ==
He supervised eight PhD students<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=149184 ''Mathematics Genealogy Project'']</ref> and a number of postdocs.<ref name="board">{{Cite web |url=http://gemma.ujf.cas.cz/~exner/board.html |title=''P. Exner's Bulletin Board'' |access-date=2019-03-18 |archive-date=2020-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200208023657/http://gemma.ujf.cas.cz/~exner/board.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Member of several professional societies,<ref name="personal"/> he served on the Executive Committee of the [[European Mathematical Society]] in 2002-10, later in 2015-18 as the EMS president.<ref>[http://euro-math-soc.eu/news/15/01/6/welcome-message-ems-president-pavel-exner ''European Mathematical Society'']</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yMMQJRaY3to ''Interview Pavel Exner - Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques'']</ref>

He served on [[IUPAP]] commission for mathematical physics (2002-08),<ref name="personal"/><ref>[http://iupap.org/about-us/executive-council/executive-council-officers-2014-2017/officers-archive-october-2002-2014/executive-council-officers-archive-2005-2008/''International Union of Pure and Applied Physics'']</ref> and [[International_Association_of_Mathematical_Physics|International Association for Mathematical Physics]] where he was President in 2009-11<ref>[[International Association of Mathematical Physics|''International Association of Mathematical Physics (IAMP)'']]</ref>{{Circular reference|date=July 2019}}. 

In 2005 he became a founding member of the [[European Research Council]],<ref>[https://erc.europa.eu/about-erc/erc-president-and-scientific-council ''European Research Council'']</ref> in 2011-14 he served as its Vicepresident for the Physical Sciences and Engineering Domain.<ref>[http://euro-math-soc.eu/news/11/04/14/pavel-exner-new-vice-president-european-research-council-erc ''European Mathematical Society'']</ref>

Member of several editorial boards, organizer of numerous conferences including the QMath series<ref>[http://gemma.ujf.cas.cz/~exner/conf_mat.html''QMath - Mathematical Results in Quantum Theory'']</ref> and the [[International Congress on Mathematical Physics]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://icmp.ujf.cas.cz/ |title=''XVI International Congress on Mathematical Physics, 2009'' |access-date=2012-03-31 |archive-date=2012-11-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121108032125/http://icmp.ujf.cas.cz/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> in 2009.

== Selected writings ==
* P. Exner: Open Quantum Systems and Feynman Integrals, D. Reidel, Dordrecht 1985. https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9789027716781 
* J. Blank, P. Exner, M. Havlíček: Hilbert-Space Operators in Quantum Physics. Second edition, revised and extended, Springer, Dordrecht 2008. https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9781402088698
* P. Exner, H. Kovařík: Quantum Waveguides, Springer International, Heidelberg 2015.  https://www.springer.com/us/book/9783319185750
* J.F. Brasche, P. Exner, Yu.A. Kuperin, P. Šeba: Schrödinger operators with singular interactions, J. Math.  Anal.  Appl. 184 (1994), 112-139. https://doi.org/10.1006/jmaa.1994.1188
* P. Duclos, P. Exner: Curvature-induced bound states in quantum waveguides in two and three dimensions, Rev. Math. Phys. 7 (1995), 73-102. https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0129055X95000062
* P. Exner, O. Post: Convergence of spectra of graph-like thin manifolds, J. Geom.  Phys. 54 (2005), 77-115. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geomphys.2004.08.003
